verses.zh: 所罗门建造耶和华殿和王宫，并一切所愿意建造的都完毕了，
verses.en: After Solomon finished building the Lord’s temple, the royal palace, and all the other construction projects he had planned,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and all the desire of Solomon which he wanted to do.”

verses.zh: 耶和华就二次向所罗门显现，如先前在基遍向他显现一样，
verses.en: the Lord appeared to Solomon a second time, in the same way he had appeared to him at Gibeon.[NOTE:1]
notes: In the same way he had appeared to him at Gibeon. See 1 Kgs 3:5.

verses.zh: 对他说：「你向我所祷告祈求的，我都应允了。我已将你所建的这殿分别为圣，使我的名永远在其中；我的眼、我的心也必常在那里。
verses.en: The Lord said to him, “I have answered[NOTE:1] your prayer and your request for help that you made to me. I have consecrated this temple you built by making it my permanent home;[NOTE:2] I will be constantly present there.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “I have heard.”
Heb “by placing my name there perpetually” (or perhaps, “forever”).
Heb “and my eyes and my heart will be there all the days.”

verses.zh: 你若效法你父大卫，存诚实正直的心行在我面前，遵行我一切所吩咐你的，谨守我的律例典章，
verses.en: You must serve me with integrity and sincerity, just as your father David did. Do everything I commanded and obey my rules and regulations.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “As for you, if you walk before me, as David your father walked, in integrity of heart and in uprightness, by doing all which I commanded you, [and] you keep my rules and my regulations.” Verse 4 is actually a lengthy protasis (“if” section) of a conditional sentence, the apodosis (“then” section) of which appears in v. 5.

verses.zh: 我就必坚固你的国位在以色列中，直到永远，正如我应许你父大卫说：『你的子孙必不断人坐以色列的国位。』
verses.en: Then I will allow your dynasty to rule over Israel permanently,[NOTE:1] just as I promised your father David, ‘You will not fail to have a successor on the throne of Israel.’[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “I will establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel forever.”
Heb “there will not be cut off from you a man from upon the throne of Israel.”

verses.zh: 倘若你们和你们的子孙转去不跟从我，不守我指示你们的诫命律例，去事奉敬拜别神，
verses.en: “But if you or your sons ever turn away from me, fail to obey the regulations and rules I instructed you to keep,[NOTE:1] and decide to serve and worship other gods,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “which I placed before you.”
Heb “and walk and serve other gods and bow down to them.”

verses.zh: 我就必将以色列人从我赐给他们的地上剪除，并且我为己名所分别为圣的殿也必舍弃不顾，使以色列人在万民中作笑谈，被讥诮。
verses.en: then I will remove Israel from the land[NOTE:1] I have given them, I will abandon this temple I have consecrated with my presence,[NOTE:2] and Israel will be mocked and ridiculed[NOTE:3] among all the nations.
notes: Heb “I will cut off Israel from upon the surface of the land.”

Instead of “I will send away,” the parallel text in 2 Chr 7:20 has “I will throw away.” The two verbs sound very similar in Hebrew, so the discrepancy is likely due to an oral transmissional error.tn Heb “and the temple which I consecrated for my name I will send away from before my face.”
Heb “will become a proverb and a taunt,” that is, a proverbial example of destruction and an object of reproach.

verses.zh: 这殿虽然甚高，将来经过的人必惊讶、嗤笑，说：『耶和华为何向这地和这殿如此行呢？』
verses.en: This temple will become a heap of ruins;[NOTE:1] everyone who passes by it will be shocked and will hiss out their scorn,[NOTE:2] saying, ‘Why did the Lord do this to this land and this temple?’
notes: Heb “and this house will be high [or elevated].” The statement makes little sense in this context, which predicts the desolation that judgment will bring. Some treat the clause as concessive, “Even though this temple is lofty [now].” Others, following the lead of several ancient versions, emend the text to, “this temple will become a heap of ruins.”
Heb “hiss,” or perhaps “whistle.” This refers to a derisive sound one would make when taunting an object of ridicule.

verses.zh: 人必回答说：『是因此地的人离弃领他们列祖出埃及地之耶和华―他们的　神，去亲近别神，事奉敬拜他，所以耶和华使这一切灾祸临到他们。』」
verses.en: Others will then answer,[NOTE:1] ‘Because they abandoned the Lord their God, who led their ancestors[NOTE:2] out of Egypt. They embraced other gods whom they worshiped and served.[NOTE:3] That is why the Lord has brought all this disaster down on them.’”
notes: Heb “and they will say.”
Heb “fathers.”
Heb “and they took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them.”

verses.zh: 所罗门建造耶和华殿和王宫，这两所二十年才完毕了。
verses.en: After 20 years, during which Solomon built the Lord’s temple and the royal palace,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the two houses, the house of the Lord and the house of the king.”

verses.zh: 泰尔王希兰曾照所罗门所要的，资助他香柏木、松木，和金子；所罗门王就把加利利地的二十座城给了希兰。
verses.en: King Solomon gave King Hiram of Tyre[NOTE:1] 20 towns in the region of Galilee, because Hiram had supplied Solomon with cedars, evergreens, and all the gold he wanted.
notes: For location see Map1-A2; Map2-G2; Map4-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.

verses.zh: 希兰从泰尔出来，察看所罗门给他的城邑，就不喜悦，
verses.en: When Hiram went out from Tyre to inspect the towns Solomon had given him, he was not pleased with them.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “they were not agreeable in his eyes.”

verses.zh: 说：「我兄啊，你给我的是甚么城邑呢？」他就给这城邑之地起名叫迦步勒，直到今日。
verses.en: Hiram asked,[NOTE:1] “Why did you give me these towns, my friend?”[NOTE:2] He called that area the region of Cabul, a name which it has retained to this day.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and he said.”
Heb “my brother.” Kings allied through a parity treaty would sometimes address each other as “my brother.” See 1 Kgs 20:32-33.

Heb “he called them the land of Cabul to this day.” The significance of the name is unclear, though it appears to be disparaging. The name may be derived from a root, attested in Akkadian and Arabic, meaning “bound” or “restricted.” Some propose a wordplay, pointing out that the name “Cabul” sounds like a Hebrew phrase meaning, “like not,” or “as good as nothing.”

verses.zh: 希兰给所罗门一百二十他连得金子。
verses.en: Hiram had sent to the king 120 talents[NOTE:1] of gold.
notes: The Hebrew term כִּכָּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or to a standard unit of weight, generally regarded as a talent. Since the accepted weight for a talent of metal is about 75 pounds, this would have amounted to about 9,000 pounds of gold (cf. NCV, NLT); CEV “five tons”; TEV “4,000 kilogrammes.”

verses.zh: 所罗门王挑取服苦的人，是为建造耶和华的殿、自己的宫、米罗、耶路撒冷的城墙、夏琐、米吉多，并基色。
verses.en: Here are the details concerning the work crews[NOTE:1] King Solomon conscripted[NOTE:2] to build the Lord’s temple, his palace, the terrace, the wall of Jerusalem,[NOTE:3] and the cities of[NOTE:4] Hazor,[NOTE:5] Megiddo,[NOTE:6] and Gezer.
notes: The work crews. This Hebrew word מַס (mas) refers to a group of laborers conscripted for royal or public service.
Heb “raised up.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
The words “the cities of” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
For location see Map1-D2; Map2-D3; Map3-A2; Map4-C1.
For location see Map1-D4; Map2-C1; Map4-C2; Map5-F2; Map7-B1.

verses.zh: 先前埃及王法老上来攻取基色，用火焚烧，杀了城内居住的迦南人，将城赐给他女儿所罗门的妻作妆奁。
verses.en: (Pharaoh, king of Egypt, had attacked and captured Gezer. He burned it and killed the Canaanites who lived in the city. He gave it as a wedding present to his daughter, who had married Solomon.)

verses.zh: 所罗门建造基色、下伯・和仑、
verses.en: Solomon built up Gezer, lower Beth Horon,

verses.zh: 巴拉，并国中旷野里的达莫，
verses.en: Baalath, Tadmor in the wilderness,[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew text has “in the wilderness, in the land.”

verses.zh: 又建造所有的积货城，并屯车和马兵的城，与耶路撒冷、黎巴嫩，以及自己治理的全国中所愿建造的。
verses.en: all the storage cities that belonged to him,[NOTE:1] and the cities where chariots and horses were kept.[NOTE:2] He built whatever he wanted in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and throughout his entire kingdom.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “to Solomon.” The proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“him”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “the cities of the chariots and the cities of the horses.”
Heb “and the desire of Solomon which he desired to build in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all the land of his kingdom.”

verses.zh: 至于国中所剩下不属以色列人的亚摩利人、赫人、比利洗人、希未人、耶布斯人，
verses.en: Now several non-Israelite peoples were left in the land after the conquest of Joshua, including the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “all the people who were left from the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who were not from the sons of Israel.”

verses.zh: 就是以色列人不能灭尽的，所罗门挑取他们的后裔作服苦的奴仆，直到今日。
verses.en: Their descendants remained in the land (the Israelites were unable to wipe them out completely). Solomon conscripted them for his work crews, and they continue in that role to this very day.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “their sons who were left after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel were unable to wipe out, and Solomon raised them up for a crew of labor to this day.”

verses.zh: 惟有以色列人，所罗门不使他们作奴仆，乃是作他的战士、臣仆、统领、军长、车兵长、马兵长。
verses.en: Solomon did not assign Israelites to these work crews;[NOTE:1] the Israelites served as his soldiers, attendants, officers, charioteers, and commanders of his chariot forces.[NOTE:2]
notes: These work crews. The work crews referred to here must be different than the temporary crews described in 5:13-16.
Heb “officers of his chariots and his horses.”

verses.zh: 所罗门有五百五十督工的，监管工人。
verses.en: These men were also in charge of Solomon’s work projects; there were a total of 550 men who supervised the workers.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “these [were] the officials of the governors who were over the work belonging to Solomon, five hundred fifty, the ones ruling over the people, the ones doing the work.”

verses.zh: 法老的女儿从大卫城搬到所罗门为她建造的宫里。那时，所罗门才建造米罗。
verses.en: Solomon built the terrace as soon as Pharaoh’s daughter moved up from the City of David[NOTE:1] to the palace Solomon built for her.[NOTE:2]
notes: The phrase City of David refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See 2 Sam 5:7.
Heb “As soon as Pharaoh’s daughter went up from the City of David to her house which he built for her, then he built the terrace.”

verses.zh: 所罗门每年三次在他为耶和华所筑的坛上献燔祭和平安祭，又在耶和华面前的坛上烧香。这样，他建造殿的工程完毕了。
verses.en: Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings[NOTE:1] on the altar he had built for the Lord, burning incense along with them before the Lord. He made the temple his official worship place.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “tokens of peace”; NIV, TEV “fellowship offerings.”
Heb “and he made complete the house.”

verses.zh: 所罗门王在以东地红海边，靠近以禄的以旬・迦别制造船只。
verses.en: King Solomon also built ships[NOTE:1] in Ezion Geber, which is located near Elat in the land of Edom, on the shore of the Red Sea.
notes: Or “a fleet” (in which case “ships” would be implied).

verses.zh: 希兰差遣他的仆人，就是熟悉泛海的船家，与所罗门的仆人一同坐船航海。
verses.en: Hiram sent his fleet and some of his sailors, who were well acquainted with the sea, to serve with Solomon’s men.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and Hiram sent with the fleet his servants, men of ships, [who] know the sea, [to be] with the servants of Solomon.”

verses.zh: 他们到了俄斐，从那里得了四百二十他连得金子，运到所罗门王那里。
verses.en: They sailed[NOTE:1] to Ophir, took from there 420 talents[NOTE:2] of gold, and then brought them to King Solomon.
notes: Heb “went.”

The Hebrew term כִּכָּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or to a standard unit of weight, generally regarded as a talent. Since the accepted weight for a talent of metal is about 75 pounds, this would have amounted to about 31,500 pounds of gold (cf. NCV); CEV, NLT “sixteen tons”; TEV “more than 14,000 kilogrammes.”
